key_insight: ISLA builds coordinate-free, measure-weighted attention for boundary-driven PDEs to preserve physical symmetries and improve robustness to boundary resampling.
engineering_relevance: It supports CFD surrogates that remain consistent across changes in pose, declared units, and boundary discretization, with predictions independent of other queried points.
method: Use distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors instead of feeding coordinates to learned operations.
Weight boundary sums by quadrature and normalize lengths using a boundary-derived scale.
Predict interior fields through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel with independent queries.
evidence_signal: On AeroZoo’s 2,816 flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors were at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline’s; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranked second to GLOBE.
watch_item: The stated rigid-motion, reflection, unit, and mesh-consistency guarantees require every boundary cell to be a token and an exact boundary read; computational trade-offs need assessment.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
